stories.headline: President Kast launches Border Shield Plan with trench construction on Peru border
stories.summary: President José Antonio Kast began construction of trenches, walls and barriers along Chile's northern border with Peru as part of the 'Plan Escudo Fronterizo' to combat illegal immigration, drug trafficking and organized crime. The plan includes military deployment and physical infrastructure.

The plan aims to boost investment and economic growth with over 40 measures across different sectors.

stories.headline: Kast debuts with high approval ratings in early polls
stories.summary: Multiple polls show President Kast beginning his term with approval ratings between 46-57%, outperforming the initial ratings of his predecessor Gabriel Boric. The polls also show high expectations for his performance on security and economic issues, though he also records higher disapproval than previous presidents at this point.

stories.headline: Death of Carabinero Javier Figueroa after shooting in Puerto Varas
stories.summary: Sargento Segundo Javier Figueroa Manquemilla died after being shot in the head during a police operation in Puerto Varas on March 11. After eight days hospitalized with brain death, he passed away on March 19. President Kast attended his funeral and declared three days of national mourning. The investigation continues with no arrests made.

stories.headline: Police shooting of civilian in San Bernardo sparks controversy
stories.summary: A 26-year-old man was shot and killed by plainclothes Carabineros during a traffic stop in San Bernardo on March 13. Neighbors dispute the official version, claiming the officers wore no identification and the victim fled thinking it was a robbery attempt. The incident has raised questions about police procedures.

The office aims to continue contributing to the country's development.

stories.headline: Codelco production drops sharply in January after December spike
stories.summary: State copper company Codelco reported its fourth-lowest monthly production of the decade in January with 91,000 tons, a 47% drop from December's 172,300 tons. The sharp decline has raised questions about the validity of the December production spike that helped the company meet its 2025 targets.

stories.headline: Controversy over possible pardons for military and police convicted during 2019 protests
stories.summary: President Kast suggested he may consider pardons for military and police personnel convicted of crimes during the 2019 social unrest. The proposal generated strong reactions from the opposition and civil society, with criticism that it could affect victims of human rights violations during those protests.

stories.headline: Foreign investment in Chile shows positive results for 2025
stories.summary: Foreign direct investment in Chile reached US$14.152 billion in 2025, a 13% increase from the previous year. January 2026 started strongly with US$1.815 billion, representing a 164% increase compared to the same month in 2025. The growth was driven mainly by reinvestment of profits.

stories.headline: Government budget adjustment measures announced
stories.summary: Finance Minister Jorge Quiroz announced a 3% budget cut across government ministries and an additional US$1 billion adjustment. The measures include reductions in travel expenses, personnel, and other operational costs, while prioritizing the functioning of the Armed Forces.
